title: Bordentown School, teacher Alexander Valentine, and meeting W.C. Handy
summary: He enrolled at Bordentown School to join its travelling band, studied under Alexander Valentine, and was turned away by W.C. Handy when seeking work as a copyist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So Bordentown School up in Bordentown, New Jersey, which was about 19 miles from Trenton, had a band that used to travel all over the state, they came to our school, and after hearing this band I just had to go. Fortunately, my parents were able to send me to this school. And that was my beginning as a musician. My teacher there was Alexander Valentine, who had been to Europe with Jim Europe. Everybody remembers Jim Europe.

Well, he had been the trombone player in the Jim Europe band, and he and W.C. Handy had been great friends. And I remember when I got out of high school and got my little piece of paper, I thought... You know, I had studied composition and arranging and copying music; I thought I could get a job as a copyist. So he gave me a note to meet Mr. Handy; I think he was at 1619 Broadway in New York. So I go to Mr. Handy's office, and I hand him my little piece of paper, and he studied me a long time and

said, "You know, son, this office is just a front; I just come here to get away from home. I've been making my living off 'St. Louis Blues' for the past forty years." So I never did get a job as a copyist, which was probably fortunate, because I continued studying.
